Published online:
    September 9, 2026

Geographic focus:
    United States

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [YES]
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
    The 30-year fixed mortgage rate rose to 6.85% (week ended Sept 4), its highest since June 2025, driven by rising Treasury yields. Key pressures include a US-Iran conflict stoking oil/inflation fears, federal debt exceeding $40T, and AI infrastructure capital demand. Refinancing fell 6.2% WoW; total mortgage applications down 2.7%. The 10-year yield is approaching 4.8%. Upcoming PPI (Thu) and CPI (Fri) prints will likely determine the Fed's posture at the Sept 15-16 meeting. Markets currently price a hike as more probable than a hold; a Fed cut — as pushed by Trump — is off the table.

Q01. Is the content's main message on the US economy, US yields, US interest rates?
Relevance: YES (primary focus is the interaction between Treasury yields, Fed policy expectations, and mortgage/borrowing costs)

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: 65 (meaningfully hawkish — traders lean toward a hike, 10-year yield near multi-year highs at ~4.8%, inflation persistently above 2% for 5.5 years, no cut in sight; only downside risk is an imminent soft CPI/PPI that could shift sentiment)
